claims.text: The target material is an equiatomic quaternary high-entropy alloy with an FCC structure.
Atomic-size mismatch among the constituent elements produces severe lattice distortion.
High-density forest dislocations are a structural mediator of deformation in the target alloy.
Interactions between dislocations and severe lattice-distortion fields create a high Peierls barrier and high friction stress.
Yield strength becomes insensitive to strain rate above an approximately 10^-2 s^-1 threshold.
The loss of strain-rate sensitivity is caused by saturation of thermally activated dislocation glide.
Increasing strain rate causes the dominant mechanism to shift from thermally activated dislocation glide to athermal glide.
At low strain rates, dislocations move by thermal activation over local barriers created by solute atoms.
At high strain rates, insufficient activation time requires stress to approach the athermal Peierls limit.
Once the athermal limit is reached, further increases in strain rate do not significantly increase yield strength.
Phase-transformation mechanisms typically have strain-rate dependencies or hysteresis distinct from saturated dislocation glide.
Yield strength increases linearly with logarithmic strain rate at low rates.
The yield-strength-versus-log-strain-rate curve develops a zero-slope plateau at high rates.
Post-deformation microscopy will show high dislocation densities and slip bands.
Tensile deformation will not produce new HCP or BCC phases.
CoCrFeMnNi alloys have been observed to exhibit strain-rate strengthening until an athermal limit is reached.
Sufficiently low stacking-fault energy can enable stress-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Sufficiently low stacking-fault energy can make deformation twinning compete with or dominate dislocation glide.
The critical strain-rate threshold depends strongly on elemental composition and lattice-distortion magnitude.
The appearance of new non-FCC diffraction peaks during deformation would identify a phase transformation and falsify the dislocation-only hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The plateau is said to begin above approximately 10^-2 s^-1, but the experiment labels 10^-3 s^-1 as a rate where the plateau is predicted; 10^-3 s^-1 lies below the stated threshold.
